newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares shed 2.65 pct in absence of package.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares shed 2.65 pct in absence of package.

text.p: Delhi shares closed sharply lower in brisk trade on Friday as speculators, disappointed that the government did not announce a large package of measures this week to bolster capital markets, sold stock, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 19.90 points, or 2.65 percent, lower at 731.65.
"Speculators who were highly optimistic about the economic package were disappointed as their expectations did not materialise and made heavy selling," said Shree Bhagwan of brokers Means Leasing.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda left on Friday on a week-long trip to attend the annual World Economic Forum summit at Davos. Contrary to market expectations, he did not announce any new steps to bolster the capital markets before leaving.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Thursday that decisions already taken this month by the government to spur the economy amounted to a package of economic reforms.
Reliance Industries fell 9.25 rupees to 267.75 on selling by speculators and financial institutions, brokers said.
State Bank of India slipped 18 rupees to 275.
ITC dropped 18.50 rupees to 388.50 on foreign selling.
Larsen and Toubro slumped 12 rupees to 236.
